title: Northbridge Health - Redwood Private on-prem POC scoping (offline install + verification)
summary: Northbridge Health and Redwood aligned on POC scope for Redwood Private on-prem in an offline/controlled network. Customer outlined a 2-environment setup (non-prod + prod-like) with no outbound internet, strict artifact intake, and a requirement to verify installer + artifacts before install. Redwood described the offline bundle approach, expected documentation package (hashes/SBOM/audit logs), and who typically owns verification (customer security + platform team; Redwood provides signed bundles and verification tooling). Next steps include Redwood sending a POC plan, documentation list, and a draft bill of materials for artifacts; customer to confirm intake process, OS/Kubernetes versions, and which team will run verification during maintenance windows.
topics: On-prem / offline environment constraints (no outbound, controlled ingress)
Installer + artifact verification ownership and workflow
Required security documentation (SBOM, hashes, signing, audit logs)
Support model and escalation during install week
questions: Can Redwood provide a signed offline bundle and a standalone verify command that runs without internet access?
How does Redwood handle key rotation for signing in air-gapped environments?
What logs are generated when verification succeeds/fails and can they be exported to SIEM?
Who is responsible for validating container images and Helm charts—Redwood or Northbridge?
What minimum Kubernetes version and OS baseline does the on-prem package support?
action_items: Redwood (Colin O'Donnell): Send POC scoping doc with recommended environment sizing, prerequisites (K8s, storage, GPU), and an offline installation flow by 2025-11-07
Redwood (Markus Klein): Send documentation checklist (signing approach overview, SBOM availability, audit log event list, support contacts) by 2025-11-07
Redwood (Bruno Silva): Draft day-by-day install week plan (who is on-call, what artifacts are needed ahead of time, validation steps) by 2025-11-10
Northbridge (Nina Alvarez): Confirm Kubernetes distro/version, container runtime, and available ingress options (NLB/HAProxy) by 2025-11-08
Northbridge (Raj Patel): Confirm internal artifact intake process (USB/media scanning, checksum verification standards, allowed crypto) and who signs off by 2025-11-12
Northbridge (Emily Chen): Identify POC app/workload and target throughput/latency goals for acceptance by 2025-11-12
next_steps: Redwood to share POC scope + prerequisites + offline verification workflow
Northbridge to confirm environment details and security intake requirements
Schedule a 60-min technical deep dive on verification/audit logging + key rotation
Target tentative POC kickoff week of 2025-12-01 pending procurement + access approvals
transcript:
Meeting: Northbridge Health - Redwood Private on-prem POC scoping (offline install + verification)
Recorded: 2025-11-05 14:00 ET
Duration: 53 min
Attendees (Redwood): Markus Klein, Colin O'Donnell, Bruno Silva
Attendees (Northbridge Health): Emily Chen, Raj Patel, Nina Alvarez, Tom Weaver

00:00 Markus Klein: Alright, hey everyone. Thanks for making the time. This is Markus from Redwood. Goal today is POC scoping for Redwood Private on-prem, specifically your offline install and what you need from us on verification and documentation. Colin is our solutions engineer, and Bruno from PS is here too.
00:15 Emily Chen: Great. Yeah, thanks Markus. We can jump in. We’re trying to get this POC done before end of year if we can, but we’re in a… let’s call it controlled network environment.
00:27 Raj Patel: Controlled is a polite word. No outbound internet. Everything comes in through our intake process.
00:33 Markus Klein: Yep, understood. That’s becoming more common for Private. Nina, Tom, good to meet you as well.
00:40 Nina Alvarez: Hi.
00:41 Tom Weaver: Hello.

00:45 Markus Klein: Maybe Emily, can you give the two-minute on the target use case and what “POC success” looks like?
00:52 Emily Chen: Sure. We have a patient communications workflow and a clinician summarization workflow. For POC we probably keep it to one, but we need to prove we can run it on-prem, integrate with our identity, and satisfy security that the installation process doesn’t pull anything from the internet and that we can attest to what got installed.
01:15 Emily Chen: Also we need predictable performance. Not necessarily max throughput, but we can’t have “surprise downloads” or “phone home”.
01:23 Markus Klein: Makes sense. Raj, anything to add on security acceptance criteria?
01:27 Raj Patel: Yeah. We need artifact provenance. So: what is being installed, hashes, signatures, and ideally SBOM. And during install, verification must fail closed. Meaning if something is off, it stops. We also want audit logs for the verification steps. If we have to use a break-glass option, that needs to be obvious and logged.
01:49 Colin O'Donnell: That all tracks with what we’ve been designing. For Private we package an offline bundle—installer plus charts/manifests plus image references and runtime artifacts—and we include a manifest with hashes. The key point is: the manifest itself is signed. Then the installer verifies signature + hashes before it proceeds.
02:10 Nina Alvarez: When you say “signed,” is it like a cert chain thing or… like GPG?
02:14 Colin O'Donnell: Good question. For POC, we can keep it at the conceptual level: Redwood signs with a release signing key, and the installer has a trust store of Redwood public keys. Verification uses that trust root. We can share details in a follow-up, including how key rotation works.
02:31 Raj Patel: We’ll need details. Our crypto policy is picky.
02:34 Markus Klein: Understood. We’ll send a doc pack.

02:38 Tom Weaver: I’m mostly listening, but timeline wise—what are you thinking? We’ve got procurement gates, but for POC we can sometimes do a pilot agreement.
02:46 Markus Klein: Totally. We were thinking: this week we define scope and prerequisites. Next week we do a technical deep dive and finalize the artifact list. Then target kickoff early December—week of Dec 1—assuming environments are ready.
03:03 Emily Chen: That’s probably realistic. We can stand up a non-prod cluster sooner. The prod-like environment might not be ready until mid-December.
03:12 Bruno Silva: For POC we usually do a two-stage: install in non-prod, validate, then repeat in prod-like with the same bundle. That also exercises your intake process.
03:22 Nina Alvarez: Our intake process is… slow. Things come in on encrypted media, get malware scanned, then we compute checksums, then we move it to the internal repo.
03:32 Raj Patel: And we need the vendor to provide published checksums and preferably a signature we can validate offline.
03:38 Colin O'Donnell: Right. So we can provide: (1) the offline bundle itself, (2) a detached signature file for the manifest, (3) the public key / certificate chain we expect you to trust, and (4) a verification command that prints “OK” or explicit errors.
03:56 Emily Chen: Who runs the verification? In our org, security wants to sign off, but platform ops has the keys to the kingdom.
04:03 Markus Klein: Typically the customer platform team runs it as part of the maintenance window, but security defines the policy and reviews the output. We’ll provide the tooling and docs and can be on a screenshare for the first run.
04:16 Raj Patel: As long as it’s auditable. We need to show that we validated the signature and the hashes *before* install.
04:24 Bruno Silva: We can build the runbook to include the exact commands and where logs land on disk. Then your team can attach that to the change record.

04:35 Nina Alvarez: Can I ask a dumb question: does the installer require Docker pull access to anything? Because there’s no pull to public registries.
04:43 Colin O'Donnell: Not dumb. In offline mode, it should never try to pull externally. We provide either images in a tarball or you mirror them into your internal registry, and the charts point to that. The installer can be configured to strictly not attempt outbound.
05:01 Nina Alvarez: Okay. We can do internal registry. But it needs to be clear what images, tags, digests.
05:07 Colin O'Donnell: Yep—image list is part of the manifest. Digests included.
05:11 Raj Patel: Do you sign the images themselves?
05:13 Colin O'Donnell: For the POC, we sign the bundle manifest that includes the digests and hashes. That provides integrity for the set. We can talk about image signing roadmap, but the immediate control is: signed manifest + digest pinning + hash verification.
05:30 Raj Patel: Okay. We’ll want to capture that in our risk acceptance.

05:36 Markus Klein: Let’s talk environment. Nina, what’s your Kubernetes version and GPU situation?
05:42 Nina Alvarez: We’re on EKS on-prem… sorry, no. It’s OpenShift 4.13 in one site, and we also have a vanilla kubeadm cluster in another lab. For POC we should use OpenShift.
05:55 Colin O'Donnell: OpenShift is fine. We’ll need to confirm the container runtime specifics, storage class, and whether you have GPU operators already.
06:05 Emily Chen: GPUs: we have a small A10 pool in non-prod and a couple A100s in the prod-like site. But it’s shared.
06:15 Bruno Silva: For POC we can start with A10s for functional validation and basic throughput, then run a targeted benchmark on A100 for the go/no-go. We’ll provide recommended sizing and which models we can run within that.
06:29 Markus Klein: Any constraints on node access? Like can we run a privileged DaemonSet for GPU metrics?
06:35 Nina Alvarez: Privileged is possible but needs security approval.
06:38 Raj Patel: We’ll want a list of privileges and RBAC needed. Least privilege.
06:42 Colin O'Donnell: Yep. We’ll send an RBAC requirements doc.

06:48 Emily Chen: Verification and audit logs—what do we get? We need to feed some of it into Splunk.
06:55 Colin O'Donnell: The installer can write an audit event locally for “bundle verification success” and “bundle verification failure” with reason codes—like hash mismatch, unknown key, expired signature, that sort of thing.
07:09 Raj Patel: Unknown key is a big one. We do not want it to proceed.
07:13 Colin O'Donnell: Default is fail closed. If you need an override for diagnostics, it’s gated and it logs a big warning. But we can keep that off for your environment.
07:25 Emily Chen: Good.

07:27 Markus Klein: Tom, any procurement concerns about the documentation set?
07:32 Tom Weaver: We’ll need the standard stuff—SOC 2, maybe your ISO cert, and for this specific topic, something that describes the signing process. Our legal folks will ask “how do you manage keys.”
07:44 Markus Klein: We can provide an overview plus the key management policy excerpt—who can sign, how rotation works, auditability.
07:52 Raj Patel: We’re also going to ask: if your key is compromised, what happens? How do we revoke trust?
07:58 Colin O'Donnell: Good question. The installer trust store can include multiple keys so rotation doesn’t brick old installs. And you can update trust roots as part of an upgrade. For compromise, we publish a revocation notice and provide an updated trust store. In offline mode you’d ingest that update like any other artifact.
08:18 Raj Patel: We’ll need a written procedure.
08:21 Bruno Silva: We’ll include it in the runbook pack.

08:26 Emily Chen: One more thing: time. Our air-gapped environment doesn’t have NTP. Does signature verification care about time?
08:33 Colin O'Donnell: It can, depending on how the signature envelope handles validity windows. We can accommodate time-skew scenarios, but we should document it. Worst case, the verify tool reports “not yet valid” and we provide guidance. We’ll cover it in the deep dive.
08:50 Raj Patel: Please do. We’ve had cert issues before because the servers drift.

09:00 Markus Klein: Cool. Let’s narrow POC scope. I heard: install Redwood Private on OpenShift in non-prod, run one application workflow end-to-end, validate offline install and verification, and produce an evidence pack. Then optionally repeat in prod-like.
09:18 Emily Chen: Yes. Also we want to see upgrade/rollback at least once. Even if it’s minor.
09:25 Bruno Silva: Great point. We can do a simulated upgrade: install version X, then apply version X+1 offline bundle, verify, upgrade, then rollback using previous bundle. The key is the verification prevents accidental downgrade attacks, but rollback procedures exist.
09:44 Nina Alvarez: Wait, rollback is a downgrade. Won’t it block?
09:47 Colin O'Donnell: It depends. We can support rollback with explicit operator intent. The system can prevent accidental downgrades, but allow rollback with a documented process. For POC we’ll define exactly what you can do.
10:02 Raj Patel: We’ll need that to be very explicit.
10:05 Markus Klein: Yep.

10:08 [Conversation continues with detailed discussion of prerequisites, artifact intake steps, and POC scheduling.]

12:15 Nina Alvarez: On the artifact bundle, can we unpack it and inspect contents without installing?
12:20 Colin O'Donnell: Yes—there’s an “inspect” or “verify” command that prints manifest contents, versions, and signature status. That’s often used by security teams before a maintenance window.
12:34 Raj Patel: That’s what we want. We’ll run that in our staging vault environment.

14:02 Emily Chen: What do you need from us to start?
14:05 Bruno Silva: Environment details: cluster access method, storage class, internal registry URL, GPU nodes, and who will be in the install bridge. Also a list of what ports you can open internally for the UI / API.
14:22 Nina Alvarez: Internal ingress is via F5 then HAProxy. No cloud load balancer.
14:27 Colin O'Donnell: Works. We’ll just need to align on TLS termination and certs.

16:10 Raj Patel: Documentation request list, let me rattle these off: signing scheme overview, key custody policy, evidence that build pipeline is controlled, SBOM, and the audit event schema.
16:25 Markus Klein: Got it. We’ll send a checklist and what we can provide for POC vs GA.
16:32 Raj Patel: Okay.

18:40 Tom Weaver: Support wise—if we hit an issue in the install window, who do we call? We can’t open a ticket and wait two days.
18:49 Markus Klein: For POC we’ll set up a dedicated Slack or email bridge, plus an on-call schedule. Bruno’s team typically joins the install bridge live.
18:59 Bruno Silva: Yeah, we do a “white glove” install for these initial air-gapped pilots.

21:05 Emily Chen: Are you expecting us to do model downloads during POC?
21:09 Colin O'Donnell: No outbound downloads. Any models we use will be included as runtime artifacts or you can provide your own approved model package. For the first POC we’ll keep it simple and include what we need in the offline bundle.
21:24 Raj Patel: Then we need to review the model artifact too. Same rules.
21:27 Colin O'Donnell: Understood.

24:10 Nina Alvarez: What about license checks or telemetry? We can’t have any external calls.
24:16 Colin O'Donnell: In Private, telemetry can be local-only. No external calls required. We can provide an export format if you want to forward logs to Splunk, but it’s your action.
24:28 Raj Patel: Great.

29:40 Markus Klein: Let’s land on dates. Tentative: next Tuesday we do the verification deep dive—45 to 60 minutes. Then we lock prerequisites by Nov 14. Then you start environment prep. Bundle delivery by end of November, install week of Dec 1.
30:00 Emily Chen: That works as a plan.
30:03 Tom Weaver: I’ll flag procurement that we’re aiming for early December.

33:12 Raj Patel: One more—key rotation. If you rotate keys mid-POC, do we have to update the installer?
33:18 Colin O'Donnell: Ideally not. The trust store can contain multiple keys. But if your installer is older than the trust update, you may need to import a new trust root file. We’ll document the path. For POC we won’t rotate in the middle.
33:36 Raj Patel: Fine.

38:05 Emily Chen: Can we get a single “evidence pack” at the end? Like: what bundle version, manifest, signature verified, and install outputs.
38:12 Bruno Silva: Yes. We can provide a template and help you fill it with the outputs from your environment.
38:21 Markus Klein: That’ll also help Tom’s side.

45:40 Markus Klein: Recap before we drop: Redwood sends POC scope doc and docs checklist by Friday. Northbridge confirms OpenShift version, registry, and intake requirements. Next Tuesday deep dive on signing/verification and audit logging. Target kickoff week of Dec 1.
45:58 Emily Chen: Sounds good.
46:00 Raj Patel: Works.
46:01 Nina Alvarez: Yep.
46:03 Tom Weaver: Thank you.

46:06 Markus Klein: Thanks all. We’ll follow up with the notes and the proposed next meeting times.

[End of transcript]
